title: The sitter's ledger

data.source: Five toy models of attention on the breath, 4000 simulated sits per model per length, seeded. No human data. The wandering share 0.47 is Killingsworth and Gilbert (2010), quoted from memory by the lens; the 60 s mean cycle is illustrative.
data.licence: none needed (generated here from a seed)

prediction: P1: all five models give the same probe-caught share within 0.02. P2: at 30 cycles a CV rule sorts Markov from accumulation at least 90% of the time. P3: power to see the seed is below 50% at 30 cycles and above 80% at 480. P4: fatigue is read as a seed more than 20% of the time at 120 cycles, and under 10% after detrending. P5: a cut with a width cannot be told from one without (accuracy under 60% at 120 cycles).
baseline: A two-state Markov model (the plain standard model) and, as a decoy, a Markov model with fatigue and no memory.
why: Four of the lens's five predictions held and one failed. The probe figure cannot tell the models apart, the shape of the cycles can tell accumulation from a constant hazard, the seed needs about 120 cycles to show, and a pause after noticing is invisible in cycle lengths. P4 failed: fatigue fooled the naive seed test less often than predicted at 120 cycles. All of it is simulation. No sitter was measured.
claim_kind: engineering usefulness (of an instrument); simulation only

alternatives.forks: 5 settings of the free knobs (spell CV 0.3, 0.4, 0.5; Q 0.4, 0.6, 0.8): P1 to P5 held in 5, 4, 5, 0, 5 of 5

operating_characteristics: The room is an operating-characteristics study: the numbers are how often each test passes in each simulated world.
second_check: Adapted and re-run by a worker who did not write the mapping. No person has reviewed it.
variants: V-contemplative-1 (the cut has a width; museum experiment, not the owner's CRR)
